report.narrative: GMV rose 38.7685% (change_abs 88507.64) in the week of 2018-07-30 versus the prior 4-week average, but the headline change was not statistically anomalous (z_score 1.569). A scan of all segments revealed one significant root cause: the share of GMV from Santa Catarina (SC) dropped from 3.2505% to 0.502% (p_value 2.006e-11), reducing total GMV by 6975.4 (-7.8811% of the total change). All other large positive contributors (SP delta 61561.91, MG delta 11555.24, RJ delta 9258.32, telephony delta 9052.65, baby delta 5739.33) failed the significance threshold (|hist_z| < 4.25). The net increase is therefore a broad-based volume lift with no other single segment reaching statistical significance.
recommended_actions: Investigate why SC orders collapsed (logistics, seller outage, or data issue) and restore that state's contribution.
Monitor the broad-based growth in SP, MG, RJ and key categories (telephony, baby, housewares) to confirm it is sustainable and not a one-off promotion.

Monitor sports_leisure GMV share in the next two weeks to confirm whether the dip was a one-off or a trend.

recommended_actions: No action required for this week; GMV is stable.

report.narrative: AOV in the week of 2018-04-23 was R$162.35, a 2.8% drop versus the prior 4-week average of R$167.00, but the change is not statistically anomalous (z = -1.63). Segment scans flagged several product categories and states with notable shifts, yet none passed the combined significance threshold (BH q ≤ 0.05 and |hist_z| ≥ 4.25). The largest contributors were the auto category (rate effect -2.63, 57% of the total decline) and watches_gifts (rate effect -5.37, 48% of the decline), but their historical z-scores were only -2.58 and -2.91 respectively. With no segment reaching the significance bar, there is no confirmed root cause for the AOV dip.
recommended_actions: Monitor AOV in the next 2-3 weeks to see if the auto and watches_gifts rate declines persist.
If the pattern repeats, investigate pricing or assortment changes in those categories.

report.narrative: AOV fell 3.6% to R$161.0 in the week of 2018-04-23 versus the prior 4-week average of R$167.0 (e1). The drop was driven almost entirely by the watches_gifts category, whose average order value plunged from R$238.2 to R$150.0 (e6), contributing 93.5% of the total AOV decline and an estimated R$9,378 revenue impact (e4). Inside that category, the average item price dropped from R$209.1 to R$123.5 (e8), a significant rate effect (p=5.1e-08), while the category's share of orders nearly doubled from 5.0% to 9.6% (e9), a significant mix effect (p=3.7e-14). The share increase for AOV was not significant (e5), confirming the AOV decline is a pure price/rate story.
recommended_actions: Investigate why watches_gifts item prices collapsed (promotion, new low-priced SKUs, or data issue).
Monitor the category's order share; if the mix shift persists, reassess AOV targets and marketing mix.

Set up a weekly on-time-rate alert by seller_state so RS-style drops are caught before they affect the headline.

Customers in São Paulo state saw their on-time rate drop from 96.7% to 34.9%, contributing 48.1% of the decline (e9, e4). The bed_bath_table category dropped from 98.2% to 28.2% on-time, contributing 18.4% (e10, e5). Credit-card orders and first-time buyers also showed large rate deteriorations (e6, e7). The root cause is a systemic delivery failure concentrated in São Paulo sellers, affecting multiple customer states, categories, and payment types simultaneously.

report.narrative: On-time delivery rate collapsed from 93.68% to 54.79% in the week of 2018-04-23 (a 41.51 pp drop, z = -8.4424). The decline was pervasive: every major segment tested showed a statistically significant rate deterioration (all q-values < 0.05). The largest single contributor was São Paulo customers (customer_state=SP), whose on-time rate fell from 97.57% to 40.53%, accounting for 63.82% of the total change and representing ~410 fewer on-time orders. Sellers in São Paulo (seller_state=SP) saw an even steeper drop to 39.28% on-time. High-volume categories furniture_decor, auto, and telephony all fell below 50% on-time. The pattern points to a systemic logistics or carrier failure centred on São Paulo rather than a mix shift.
recommended_actions: Immediately audit carrier performance and warehouse operations in São Paulo state for the week of 2018-04-23.
Check whether a specific carrier contract, sorting hub, or weather event disrupted deliveries in SP and neighbouring states (MG, GO).
Prioritise recovery for high-impact categories (furniture_decor, auto, telephony) and payment methods (boleto) that saw the steepest rate drops.
Set up automated weekly on-time-rate alerts by state and category to catch similar systemic drops earlier.

report.narrative: On-time delivery rate collapsed from 97.2% to 51.5% in the week of 2017-07-24, a 47-percentage-point drop (e1). The decline was driven almost entirely by a rate effect inside São Paulo sellers, whose on-time rate fell from 97.3% to 33.4% and accounted for 100% of the total change (e15). Every major segment — credit-card orders, new customers, São Paulo customers, bed-bath-table and housewares categories, Minas Gerais and Rio de Janeiro customers, sports-leisure, boleto and voucher payments, and even repeat customers — showed a statistically significant rate decline (e3–e14). The pattern is systemic across dimensions rather than isolated to one segment, pointing to a platform-wide fulfillment or logistics failure that week.
recommended_actions: Investigate the São Paulo seller fulfillment network for the week of 2017-07-24 (carrier outages, warehouse issues, staffing).
Check whether a system-wide shipping-label or tracking update was deployed that week and caused delays.
Review carrier SLA compliance reports for that week to identify the bottleneck.

report.narrative: The average review score was essentially flat week-over-week (4.105 vs 4.106 baseline, -0.11%), so the headline metric was not anomalous. However, a deep segment scan revealed a severe, statistically significant drop inside the "auto" product category: its review score fell from 4.04 to 2.08 stars (p < 0.001, q = 6e-15). This single category accounts for 1,824% of the total change (i.e., it more than offsets small improvements elsewhere) and affected roughly 71 orders this week. No other segment reached significance.
recommended_actions: Investigate the auto-category fulfilment and product-quality issues that drove reviews down to ~2 stars (e.g., shipping damage, wrong parts, seller responsiveness).
Set up an automated alert on per-category review scores so similar drops are caught before they bleed into the overall metric.

report.narrative: The average review score rose 1.1% to 4.15 stars in the week of 2018-04-23 versus the prior 4-week average of 4.11 stars. The headline change was not statistically anomalous (z = -0.73), but segment analysis revealed a significant negative rate effect in the telephony category, where the average score dropped from 4.0 to 2.4 stars (p = 8.1e-8), contributing -108% of the total change. This was offset by positive rate improvements in watches_gifts (+64% contribution, p = 0.026), furniture_decor (+39%, p = 0.031), computers_accessories (+29%, p = 0.12), and baby (+25%, p = 0.13). The telephony decline is the only segment that passes both the significance and historical-unusualness thresholds, making it the primary root cause.
recommended_actions: Investigate telephony orders in the week of 2018-04-23 for delivery issues, product defects, or seller problems that could explain the sharp review score drop.
Monitor telephony review scores weekly to detect if the low scores persist or were a one-off event.

report.narrative: AOV dropped 16.9% (from R$149.43 to R$124.12) in the week of 2017-08-14, a statistically anomalous decline (z = -6.0432). The decomposition shows 91.6% of the drop came from lower value per item. Three significant root causes were found: (1) a massive mix shift toward fashion_bags_accessories, whose order share jumped from 1.9984% to 28.098% (p = 1.802e-184), contributing 78.6043% of the AOV change and an estimated R$-27570.2 GMV impact; (2) a rate drop in seller_state SP, where AOV fell from R$142.44 to R$114.37 (p = 1.24e-08), contributing 84.7142% and R$-29713.2 impact; (3) a rate drop among new customers (is_repeat_customer=0), AOV from R$148.92 to R$124.45 (p = 2.781e-06), contributing 92.2035% and R$-32340.07 impact. The mix shift and the two rate declines overlap in the same orders, so impacts are not additive.
recommended_actions: Investigate why fashion_bags_accessories surged to 28% of orders this week (promotion, new seller onboarding, catalog change) and assess if the low AOV is sustainable or a one-off.
Diagnose the SP seller AOV decline: check for price changes, discount campaigns, or a shift toward lower-priced sub-categories within SP.
Review new-customer acquisition channels this week; the AOV drop among first-time buyers may signal a low-ticket acquisition campaign or onboarding friction.

report.narrative: AOV rose 5.9% to R$169.15 in the week of 2017-05-08 versus the prior 4-week average of R$159.75. report.narrative: AOV dropped 11.0% (R$ 18.37) in the week of 2018-04-23 versus the prior 4-week average, a statistically anomalous decline (z = -3.54). The primary driver was a mix shift: electronics orders surged from 2.8% to 19.6% of all orders, and because electronics carry a lower AOV (R$ 70.10 vs R$ 71.90 baseline), this alone explains 88.7% of the total AOV drop (R$ -32,657.91 impact). Simultaneously, new customers (is_repeat_customer=0), who represent 97.3% of orders, saw their AOV fall 11.0% (R$ 167.22 → R$ 148.83), contributing 97.4% of the change (R$ -35,840.18 impact). Both credit-card and boleto payment types also experienced significant rate declines (credit-card: R$ 173.09 → R$ 157.30; boleto: R$ 153.14 → R$ 122.97). The decomposition shows value per item fell 9.2% while items per order fell only 1.9%, confirming the drop is price-driven.
recommended_actions: Investigate why electronics order share jumped 7x in one week — check for a promotion, new seller onboarding, or catalog change.
Diagnose the new-customer AOV decline: review acquisition channels, first-purchase incentives, and onboarding flows that may be attracting lower-value buyers.
Monitor payment-type AOV trends weekly; the boleto drop (R$ 153.14 → R$ 122.97) may signal a shift in buyer profile or installment options.

report.narrative: AOV in the week of 2017-05-08 was R$166.54, up 4.2% from the prior 4-week average of R$159.75, but the change is not statistically anomalous (robust z = 0.31). recommended_actions: Monitor computers_accessories and SP seller share in coming weeks to confirm if the mix shift persists.
If the share shift continues, quantify its AOV impact with a controlled experiment or price-mix decomposition.

report.narrative: AOV rose 9.4% to R$158.87 in the week of 2017-08-07 versus the prior 4-week average of R$145.17, a statistically anomalous jump (z=7.93). The increase was driven almost entirely by higher value per item (+8.8%) rather than more items per order (+0.5%). Across all product categories and customer states, no individual segment showed a statistically significant rate or mix shift (all q-values > 0.05 and |hist_z| < 4.25). The uplift appears to be a broad-based, small increase spread over many segments rather than a concentrated root cause.
recommended_actions: Monitor AOV for the next 2-3 weeks to see if the elevation persists or reverts.
If the higher AOV holds, investigate whether a subtle pricing or assortment change (e.g., new higher-priced SKUs) was introduced across multiple categories.

report.narrative: The cancellation rate rose 114.7% in the week of 2017-07-24 (from 0.37% to 0.80%), but the change is not statistically anomalous (robust z = 1.05). No segment showed a significant rate or mix shift after multiple-test correction (all Benjamini-Hochberg q-values > 0.05 and historical z-scores below the 4.25 threshold). The largest contributors were new-customer orders (rate +107.9% contribution) and São Paulo sellers (rate +88.7% contribution), but neither passed significance. Therefore, the observed increase is consistent with normal week-to-week variation.
recommended_actions: Monitor cancellation rate for the next 2-3 weeks to see if the uptick persists.
If the rate remains elevated, re-run the investigation with a longer baseline to increase statistical power.
